title: Links and Navigation
subtitle: Anchor elements, URLs, internal links, external links and navigation structures.
description: Connect webpages together and build useful navigation systems.

blocks.text: Welcome to Lesson 3: Links and Navigation. This lesson follows the course dashboard topic “Links and Navigation”. The goal is to anchor elements, URLs, internal links, external links and navigation structures.. Focus on understanding when this technique is useful, what assumptions it makes, and how you can check that it is working.
An anchor element creates a link when it has a valid href. A URL may be absolute, such as a full web address, or relative to the current document or site path.

blocks.question: A link to about.html fails only after deployment in a subdirectory. What should you inspect?
options: Whether the href path resolves correctly from the deployed URL.
blocks.explanation: Relative URLs depend on the current URL or site path; test resource paths after deployment.
blocks.hint: Identify the requirement in the scenario, eliminate choices that ignore it, and choose the option that preserves correctness and maintainability.
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct. Relative URLs depend on the current URL or site path; test resource paths after deployment.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Review the requirement again. Relative URLs depend on the current URL or site path; test resource paths after deployment.

blocks.text: Application tip: in a real HTML project, choose names and structures that reveal the reason the code exists. Do not copy a snippet into a project without checking its assumptions and adapting it to the surrounding code.

blocks.question: An action deletes a record. Which element should normally represent that action?
options: A button with a clear action label.
blocks.explanation: Buttons represent actions; anchors represent navigation to a resource.
blocks.hint: Identify the requirement in the scenario, eliminate choices that ignore it, and choose the option that preserves correctness and maintainability.
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct. Buttons represent actions; anchors represent navigation to a resource.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Review the requirement again. Buttons represent actions; anchors represent navigation to a resource.

blocks.text: Use link text that describes the destination or action. “Read the installation guide” is more useful when heard out of context than “click here.” Check relative paths after deployment because a folder or filename mismatch can break navigation.

blocks.question: A group of links forms the site’s main navigation. What improves accessibility?
options: Put them in a nav landmark with a descriptive label if needed.
Make them clickable only on hover.
blocks.explanation: A nav landmark helps users identify navigation, and clear link text communicates the destination.
blocks.hint: Identify the requirement in the scenario, eliminate choices that ignore it, and choose the option that preserves correctness and maintainability.
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct. A nav landmark helps users identify navigation, and clear link text communicates the destination.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Review the requirement again. A nav landmark helps users identify navigation, and clear link text communicates the destination.

blocks.text: PAGE 3 — Apply it and check your reasoning
Links navigate to resources; buttons perform actions. Keeping these roles distinct improves keyboard interaction, accessibility, and user expectations.

blocks.question: A program repeatedly looks up a learner by a unique email address. Which structure is a natural fit?
options: A map/dictionary keyed by email, with suitable uniqueness handling.
A random number with no mapping.
A paragraph of comma-separated values that is never parsed.
A loop that guesses the correct person.
blocks.explanation: Key-value structures express lookup by identifier more directly than repeatedly scanning unrelated data.
blocks.hint: Identify the requirement in the scenario, eliminate choices that ignore it, and choose the option that preserves correctness and maintainability.
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct. Key-value structures express lookup by identifier more directly than repeatedly scanning unrelated data.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Review the requirement again. Key-value structures express lookup by identifier more directly than repeatedly scanning unrelated data.
